name: FineDB
tagline: 2013 learning project: a multi-threaded C key-value server on LMDB and nanomsg with Snappy compression.
description: FineDB is a small key-value database server written in C by Amaury Bouchard in mid-2013, mainly as a way to learn network programming, multi-threading and replication. Storage is delegated to LMDB, which provides memory-mapped B+tree pages and MVCC so readers never block the writer, while nanomsg sockets connect the connection threads to a single writer thread. Clients speak a compact binary protocol with GET, PUT, DEL, LIST, DROP, PING and database-selection commands, optional synchronous or asynchronous acknowledgement, and Snappy-compressed values; each stored value carries a replication timestamp and an expiry time. It ships a C client library and a command-line shell. Development stopped in September 2013 and the finedb.org domain is parked.
statusNote: No commits since September 2013; finedb.org is parked. LMDB itself, or servers built on it, are the maintained route.
strengths: LMDB storage gives crash-safe, memory-mapped reads that never block on writes
Clean thread design: connection threads feed one writer over nanomsg
Per-value expiry and Snappy compression in a very small codebase
weaknesses: Abandoned after a few months of development in 2013
Replication and clustering were planned but never finished
Only a C client library; no authentication
useCases: Learning how to wrap LMDB in a multi-threaded network server
Reference code for nanomsg-based internal messaging
